source.title: Auditing Reasoning-Trace Memorization Claims after Unlearning with Head-Conditioned Canaries
source.authors: Yan-Han Li; Zhi-Chao Fan; Ze-Xin Zhuang

page_placements.theme: Forgetting metrics disagree: output-level forgetting while likelihood, ranks, CoT, paraphrase or facts still carry the target (no attack)

record.file_problem: The full paper and appendices are present; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The paper directly audits whether a parser-split trace/answer gap identifies weight-level retention, and reports that fixed-weight prefill changes and parser-format drift make the interpretation non-identifying.
record.gate_note: The study tests NPO and Gradient Ascent on synthetic, LoRA-memorized canaries, plus fixed-weight prefill and teacher-forced probes. It does not test fine-tuning on unrelated examples, activation-direction ablation, quantization, jailbreaks, or other languages. Teacher-forced scores are head-conditioned measurements, not free-recall or retention estimates; the authors explicitly caution against treating them as such.
record.test_reason: The study works in a new setting: LoRA-memorized fictional authors in distilled reasoning models, unlearned with NPO or Gradient Ascent. It reports forget-set accuracy, retain accuracy and fixed-weight prefill effects that bear on A and E. Its central object, the parser-split trace/answer gap, is a related construct and belongs in fits_no_version. That makes T3 a better fit than T5: the paper's argument targets an audit metric, not a version of the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that a positive parser-split bypass gap neither identifies nor rules out hidden weight-level memorization. Fixed-weight prefill moves answer rates, with seed-dependent direction, and on Llama-8B the parser fallback alone flips the gap's sign. They recommend adding a fixed-prefill decode arm and teacher-forced scoring. They also present the teacher-forced score as a metric-stability check rather than retention evidence, and disclaim any claim about practical extraction risk.
record.recipe_differences: Uses NPO, a method named in the claim, but applies answer-span-masked unlearning to LoRA-memorized fictional biographies in reasoning models. The paper is an audit-validity study, not a broad comparison of unlearning methods or recovery attacks.
record.method_sensitivity: The prefill effect changes direction across seeds: seed 0 prefills lower answer accuracy, while seed 1 prefills raise it to 0.98–1.00. On Llama-8B the parser gap depends on the fallback convention; missing closing tags cause a parser false negative.

fits_no_version.finding: The parser-split trace/answer gap changes under fixed-weight prefill and flips from −0.92 to +0.92 under the alternative parser fallback on Llama-8B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In reasoning-model unlearning audits, parser-split trace/answer gaps depend on decoding context and parser conventions and do not by themselves identify weight-level retention.

fits_no_version.finding: Teacher-forced head-conditioned top-1 stays at 0.90–1.00 after NPO while greedy substring accuracy falls. There are no shuffled-head baselines, and the authors say this is not retention evidence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Head-conditioned teacher-forced continuation scores stay high when greedy substring accuracy drops after answer-masked NPO.

record.problems: Synthetic, small-scale fictional-author setup with one main Qwen seed and one additional seed; only two distilled models are tested. Canary prompts supply the first six tokens, so reported accuracy and teacher-forced scores are head-conditioned rather than free recall. The prefill contrast jointly changes trace presence, prefix length/style, and canary content, so it does not isolate a mechanism. Teacher-forced probes lack shuffled-head or wrong-author baselines. NPO substantially reduces Qwen retain-set accuracy, and Llama NPO does not reduce answer accuracy. Parser fallback drives the Llama sign flip.
record.rows_left_out: The detailed training-time BIO/META/NONE table is summarized in R35 rather than split into separate rows for every mode/checkpoint/metric; it uses separately trained adapters and is not a fixed-weight recovery attack. Appendix C's full prefill K-sweep is not transcribed beyond the headline K=1600 prefill results, because the main recovery/prompt result and its seed reversal are represented in R13–R18. Table 2 log-probability and perplexity values are omitted because the top-1 continuation measure already captures the reported comparison and the authors characterize the teacher-forced branch as a metric-stability check, not retention evidence.

untested.parts: Other unlearning methods (RMU/WMDP, the Harry Potter approach) are not tested. Real hazardous or copyrighted knowledge is not used, only synthetic canaries. No attack other than the trace prefill is tried. Retain utility is not measured for GA.
No relearning fine-tuning of any kind.
There is no activation-direction ablation. The teacher-forced probe and the App. D truncation analysis are explicitly disclaimed as retention evidence.
Rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages and in-context supply of the facts are not tested. Only short non-canary reasoning-trace prefills are tried.
No robust or trace-aware counter-method is tested; the authors name this as future work.

missing.what: Seed-1 autoregressive out acc at NPO K=1600 (0.68) and the seed-1 bypass gaps; these are needed as a separate A row for seed 1.
Llama-8B retain accuracy: 0.78 memorized vs 0.72 after NPO K=1600.
Prefill on the memorized adapter lowers out acc to 0.93/0.95/0.92, and on QA probes gives 0.78/0.46/0.50. These are controls showing the prefill perturbs generically.

record.verdict_notes: This is a measurement-validity paper on a synthetic, LoRA-memorized setup; NPO is masked to the answer span and the trace is never unlearned. All accuracies are head-conditioned, because six canary tokens are supplied, so chance is not a clean reference. The E evidence comes from two seeds that point in opposite directions. The trace prefill is a prompt-side intervention, but not a standard rephrasing or jailbreak attack.

versions.untested_parts: The study tests NPO and Gradient Ascent on synthetic canaries, but does not test whether a successful unlearning method across the named methods retains general ability while resisting all simple attacks. NPO does not bring Qwen answer accuracy near chance; Gradient Ascent reaches zero on the reported probes in a collapse regime. Retain utility is measured for NPO, not Gradient Ascent.
No post-unlearning fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or subset examples is performed.

No activation-direction ablation is performed, and the study does not establish that the unlearning method blocks access rather than deleting knowledge. It tests whether a parser-split gap identifies weight-level retention.

The prompt intervention is a fixed-weight change to the thinking prefill, not a systematic test of rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or ordinary in-context information. Canary prompts already supply the first six canary tokens.
No newer robust counter-method is tested against the listed attacks.

source_check.notes: Small synthetic setup: 60 fictional authors, LoRA, n=60 per cell. Probes supply the first six canary tokens, so out acc is head-conditioned. The direction of the prefill effect depends on the seed. The row unc 'unpaired CI [-0.17,+0.17]' seems to be for the BIO-vs-META contrast; the paired ∆AB CI for the seed-0 drop is [.10,.37] (Table 6). E.support[5] and E.against[9] cite rows but never name the study.

statements.correction: 2605.18891, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B, 60 LoRA-memorized fictional authors, answer-masked NPO K=1600, seed 1: BIO/META/EMPTY thinking-trace prefills raise canary out acc from 0.68 to 1.00/1.00/0.98 (App F). Seed 0: the same prefills lower it from 0.60 to 0.37/0.37/0.20 (Table 1). The six-token canary head is in the prompt. Teacher-forced top-1 on seed 1 is >=0.997.
statements.problem: The statement never names this study, but cites its R16 as support for demonstrations, role-play and few-shot prompts in PII/WMDP/BeaverTails/HP/MUSE settings. R16 is a different thing: a short non-canary thinking-trace prefill at fixed weights, with the six-token canary head supplied. On seed 0 the same prefills lower accuracy.

statements.correction: Qwen-7B, NPO K=1600, seed 0: out acc goes from 0.60 to 0.37 (BIO), 0.37 (META) and 0.20 (EMPTY). The memorized adapter under the same prefills scores 0.93/0.95/0.92. Seed 1: out acc goes from 0.68 to 1.00/1.00/0.98.
statements.problem: The statement never names this study, but cites R13-R15 as in-context, few-shot or role-play prompts that fail to restore. These are thinking-trace prefills, not those prompt types. They also lower the memorized adapter (1.00 to 0.93/0.95/0.92) and ordinary QA probes, and the authors read this as decode-time sensitivity. Seed 1 goes the other way.

statements.correction: Fixed-weight BIO/META/EMPTY prefills: Qwen-7B seed 0, memorized and NPO K=100/400/800/1600 (Table 6); Qwen-7B seed 1, NPO K=1600 (App F); Llama-8B, memorized and NPO K=1600, out acc 1.00/0.98/0.98 (Sec 4.4). No jailbreak, multi-turn or other-language prompts.
statements.problem: 'One NPO setup across two seeds' understates what was run. On seed 0, prefills were run across the whole NPO K-sweep. They were also run on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B, memorized and NPO K=1600, though NPO did not lower out acc there. The point that no jailbreak, multi-turn or other-language prompts were used is correct.

Accurate. Model, prefills and numbers are right (seed 0: 0.60 to 0.37/0.37/0.20; seed 1: 0.68 to 1.00/1.00/0.98). The factor line names seed, and each seed is a separate run of the full memorize-then-unlearn pipeline (App F).

Accurate. Teacher-forced top-1 is 0.96/0.96/0.90 on seed 0 and >=0.997 on seed 1 and on Llama. Greedy substring accuracy falls on Qwen seed 0 (1.00 to 0.60). The authors call the probe a sanity check with no shuffled-head baseline and say it is not retention evidence. Minor: cited R34 (Llama substring accuracy 0.98-1.00) does not fall.
